description: Figure 16b, titled “MMLU confidence vs. accuracy,” is a line plot that displays three distinct data series—labeled “Final Accuracy” (blue solid line with square markers), “Δ Accuracy” (orange dashed line with triangle markers), and “Initial Accuracy” (green dashed line with circle markers)—plotted against the “Initial Confidence” on the x-axis, which ranges from approximately 0.71 to 1.00 with tick marks at intervals of 0.01, and “Accuracy” on the y-axis, which ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The “Initial Accuracy” line begins near 0.4 and trends upward to near 0.85. The “Final Accuracy” line starts near 0.85, dips slightly, and then generally trends upward to near 1.0. The “Δ Accuracy” line begins near 0.0, rises to a peak near 0.25 at an initial confidence of approximately 0.79, and then declines sharply to near 0.0 by an initial confidence of approximately 0.95.
